::: {#sol-linear-input-grad}

Input $h_k$ affects every output $z_j$,
so the chain rule adds up a term for each:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\derivf{\loss}{h_k}
&= \sum_j \derivf{\loss}{z_j} \derivf{z_j}{h_k}
&& \text{(chain rule through every $z_j$)} \\
&= \sum_j \backerr_j W_{jk}
&& \text{(since $\derivf{z_j}{h_k} = W_{jk}$)} \\
&= \paren{\tp{\matr{W}} \vbackerr}_k
&& \text{(entry $k$ of a matrix-vector product)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\gradwrt{\vhidval} \loss = \tp{\matr{W}} \vbackerr$:
the [gradient](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) travels back through the layer by the transpose of its weight matrix.

:::
